metrics.formula: First click average order quantity = (products + gift cards) / orders

schemas.name: campaign_sessions
schemas.description: The `campaign_sessions` schema captures what visitors did during online store sessions that came from a marketing campaign. It carries the same engagement and funnel measures as the `sessions` schema, but only for campaign-driven traffic, with campaign, customer, device, browser, and location detail.

metrics.name: campaign_added_to_cart_rate
metrics.description: The share of online store visits from campaigns where a visitor added at least one item to cart.
metrics.formula: Campaign added to cart rate = sessions with cart additions / sessions

metrics.name: campaign_average_session_duration
metrics.description: Average duration, in seconds, of campaign-associated online store visits

metrics.name: campaign_bounce_rate
metrics.description: The share of online store visits from campaigns that ended after one pageview.
metrics.formula: Campaign bounce rate = bounces / sessions

metrics.name: campaign_bounces
metrics.description: Campaign-associated online store visits that ended after a single pageview

metrics.name: campaign_checkout_conversion_rate
metrics.description: Among campaign visits that reached checkout, this is the share that completed a purchase.
metrics.formula: Campaign checkout conversion rate = sessions that completed checkout / sessions that reached checkout

metrics.name: campaign_completed_checkout_rate
metrics.description: Among campaign visits where a visitor added an item to cart and reached checkout, this is the share that completed a purchase.
metrics.formula: Campaign completed checkout rate = sessions with cart additions that reached checkout and completed checkout / sessions with cart additions that reached checkout

metrics.name: campaign_conversion_rate
metrics.description: The share of online store visits from campaigns that ended in a completed checkout.
metrics.formula: Campaign conversion rate = sessions that completed checkout / sessions

metrics.name: campaign_online_store_visitors
metrics.description: Each visitor is counted as a single visitor across their online store visits from campaigns.

metrics.name: campaign_pageviews
metrics.description: A single online store visit from a campaign can contribute more than one pageview.

metrics.name: campaign_pageviews_per_session
metrics.description: Average number of pageviews per campaign-associated online store visit
metrics.formula: Campaign-associated store pageviews per session = pageviews / sessions

metrics.name: campaign_reached_checkout_rate
metrics.description: The share of online store visits from campaigns where the visitor reached checkout.
metrics.formula: Campaign reached checkout rate = sessions that reached checkout / sessions

metrics.name: campaign_sessions
metrics.description: One visitor can have multiple online store visits from campaigns.

metrics.name: campaign_sessions_that_completed_checkout
metrics.description: Campaign-associated online store visits in which a purchase was completed

metrics.name: campaign_sessions_that_reached_and_completed_checkout
metrics.description: Campaign-associated online store visits in which the checkout page was reached, then purchase was completed

metrics.description: Campaign-associated online store visits in which the checkout page was reached

metrics.name: ending_inventory_value
metrics.description: The cost value of stock on hand at the end of your selected period, in your store's currency. It uses the item's recorded cost and ending unit count. Untracked items, items without a recorded cost, and items with zero or negative ending stock contribute 0.

metrics.name: last_day_in_inventory

metrics.name: percent_of_inventory_sold

metrics.formula: Percent of inventory sold = inventory units sold / starting inventory units

metrics.name: sell_through_rate

metrics.formula: Sell-through rate = inventory units sold / (inventory units sold + ending inventory units)

metrics.name: duties

metrics.name: gift_card_discounts

metrics.name: gift_card_gross_sales
metrics.description: Gift card sales revenue before discounts and returns are taken out, in your store's currency. Use `gift_card_gross_sales` to see top-line gift card revenue over time.

metrics.name: gift_card_net_sales
metrics.description: Gift card sales revenue after discounts and returns are factored in, in your store's currency. Use `gift_card_net_sales` to measure gift card revenue net of those reductions.

metrics.name: gift_card_taxes

metrics.name: gross_margin
metrics.description: The share of sales kept as gross profit after cost of goods sold is factored in. Gross margin is based on sales where cost of goods sold is recorded.
metrics.formula: Gross margin = gross profit / net sales

metrics.name: gross_profit
metrics.description: Sales revenue after cost of goods sold is taken out, before other operating expenses, in your store's currency.
metrics.formula: Gross profit = net sales - cost of goods sold

metrics.name: gross_returns
metrics.description: Value of items removed from orders before discounts and taxes

metrics.name: gross_sales
metrics.description: Top-line sales revenue before discounts and returns are taken out, in your store's currency. Use `gross_sales` to see gross revenue over time or by a grouping like product or channel. It excludes taxes, shipping, duties, and fees.

metrics.name: gross_sales_reversals

metrics.name: high_fraud_risk_rate

metrics.name: line_item_discounts

metrics.name: net_items_sold
metrics.description: The number of items sold after returned or reversed quantities are factored in. Use `net_items_sold` to track product movement over time or by product.

metrics.name: net_returns
metrics.description: Value of items removed from orders after discounts, before taxes
metrics.formula: Net returns = gross returns + discounts returned

metrics.name: net_sales
metrics.description: Sales revenue after discounts and sales reversals, excluding taxes, shipping, duties, and fees, in your store's currency.
metrics.formula: Net sales = gross sales - discounts - sales reversals

metrics.name: net_sales_reversals
metrics.description: Value of items removed from orders after discounts, before taxes
metrics.formula: Net sales reversals = gross sales reversals + discount reversals

metrics.name: net_sales_with_cost_recorded
metrics.description: Product net sales where cost of goods sold is recorded, in your store's currency. Use `net_sales_with_cost_recorded` to understand the revenue base used for profit measures.

metrics.name: net_sales_without_cost_recorded

metrics.name: new_customers

metrics.name: number_of_orders_per_customer

metrics.name: order_level_discounts

metrics.name: order_sale_agreements

metrics.name: orders

metrics.name: orders_returning

metrics.name: quantity_ordered

metrics.name: returned_quantity_rate

metrics.name: returning_customers

metrics.name: returns

metrics.name: reversed_quantity

metrics.name: reversed_quantity_rate
metrics.description: Percentage of items removed from orders out of total items sold

metrics.name: sales_reversals

metrics.name: shipping_charge_discounts

metrics.name: shipping_charge_taxes

metrics.name: shipping_charges

metrics.name: shipping_reversals

metrics.name: tax_reversals

metrics.name: taxes

metrics.name: taxes_excluding_gift_cards
metrics.description: Taxes charged on sales excluding taxes from gift card sales, in your store's currency. Use `taxes_excluding_gift_cards` when you want tax amounts without gift card tax included.

metrics.name: taxes_returned
metrics.description: Tax amounts removed from orders

metrics.name: tips
metrics.description: Customer gratuities added to sales, in your store's currency. Use `tips` to track tip amounts over time or by retail location.

metrics.name: total_returns
metrics.description: Total value removed from orders, including products, shipping, taxes, and fees
metrics.formula: Total returns = net returns + shipping returned + return fees + taxes returned

metrics.name: total_sales
metrics.description: The full amount customers spent, including taxes, shipping, duties, and fees, in your store's currency.
metrics.formula: Total sales = net sales + additional fees + duties + shipping charges + taxes

metrics.name: total_sales_first_time
metrics.description: The full amount spent by customers making their first purchase, in your store's currency. Use `total_sales_first_time` to track revenue from newly acquired customers over time or by channel.

metrics.name: total_sales_returning
metrics.description: The full amount spent by customers who had bought from you before, in your store's currency. Use `total_sales_returning` to track repeat customer revenue over time or by channel.

metrics.name: total_sales_reversals
metrics.description: Total value removed from orders, including products, shipping, taxes, and fees
metrics.formula: Total sales reversals = net sales reversals + shipping reversals + sale reversal fees + tax reversals

metrics.name: total_shipping_charges
metrics.description: The full shipping amount customers spent, in your store's currency. It reflects shipping charges after shipping discounts and shipping taxes are included. Use `total_shipping_charges` to track total shipping revenue over time.
metrics.formula: Total shipping charges = shipping charges - shipping discounts + shipping taxes

metrics.name: cls_distribution
metrics.description: A breakdown of page loads by Cumulative Layout Shift, which measures how much content moves unexpectedly while the page loads. The values show measured loads, then good (0.1 or lower), needs improvement (above 0.1 through 0.25), and poor (above 0.25). Use `cls_distribution` to see how layout stability is spread across visits.

metrics.name: cls_good_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a good Cumulative Layout Shift score. Good CLS means the score is 0.1 or lower. Use `cls_good_view_count` to track stable page loads over time or by `page_type`.

metrics.name: cls_okay_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a Cumulative Layout Shift score that needs improvement. This covers CLS scores above 0.1 through 0.25. Use `cls_okay_view_count` to find pages where layout stability may need attention.

metrics.name: cls_poor_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a poor Cumulative Layout Shift score. Poor CLS means the score is above 0.25. Use `cls_poor_view_count` to spot pages with noticeable unexpected movement.

metrics.name: fcp_distribution
metrics.description: A breakdown of page loads by First Contentful Paint, which measures how quickly the first visible content appears. The values show measured loads, then good (1.8 seconds or faster), needs improvement (above 1.8 through 3 seconds), and poor (slower than 3 seconds). Use `fcp_distribution` to see how early loading speed is spread across visits.

metrics.name: fcp_good_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a good First Contentful Paint score. Good FCP means the first content appeared in 1.8 seconds or less. Use `fcp_good_view_count` to track fast initial loading over time or by `page_type`.

metrics.name: fcp_okay_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a First Contentful Paint score that needs improvement. This covers first content appearing after 1.8 seconds through 3 seconds. Use `fcp_okay_view_count` to find pages where initial loading could be faster.

metrics.name: fcp_p50_ms
metrics.description: The median First Contentful Paint time, in milliseconds. Half of measured page loads had first content appear at or below this value. Use `fcp_p50_ms` to track typical initial loading speed.

metrics.name: fcp_p75_ms
metrics.description: The 75th percentile First Contentful Paint time, in milliseconds. Most measured page loads had first content appear at or below this value. Use `fcp_p75_ms` to monitor the loading experience for a broad share of visitors.

metrics.name: fcp_p90_ms
metrics.description: The 90th percentile First Contentful Paint time, in milliseconds. This shows the initial loading time that 90% of measured page loads met or beat. Use `fcp_p90_ms` to watch slower loading experiences.

metrics.name: fcp_p99_ms
metrics.description: The 99th percentile First Contentful Paint time, in milliseconds. This shows the initial loading time that nearly all measured page loads met or beat. Use `fcp_p99_ms` to investigate the slowest experiences.

metrics.name: fcp_poor_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events in which the first visible content appeared after more than 1.8 seconds.

metrics.name: inp_distribution
metrics.description: A breakdown of page loads by Interaction to Next Paint, which measures how quickly a page responds after visitor interactions. The values show measured loads, then good (200 milliseconds or faster), needs improvement (above 200 through 500 milliseconds), and poor (slower than 500 milliseconds). Use `inp_distribution` to see how responsiveness is spread across visits.

metrics.name: inp_good_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a good Interaction to Next Paint score. Good INP means the page responded in 200 milliseconds or less. Use `inp_good_view_count` to track responsive experiences over time or by `page_type`.

metrics.name: inp_okay_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with an Interaction to Next Paint score that needs improvement. This covers response times above 200 through 500 milliseconds. Use `inp_okay_view_count` to find pages where interactions may feel delayed.

metrics.name: inp_p50_ms
metrics.description: The median Interaction to Next Paint time, in milliseconds. Half of measured page loads responded to interactions at or below this value. Use `inp_p50_ms` to track typical page responsiveness.

metrics.name: inp_p75_ms
metrics.description: The 75th percentile Interaction to Next Paint time, in milliseconds. Most measured page loads responded to interactions at or below this value. Use `inp_p75_ms` to monitor responsiveness for a broad share of visitors.

metrics.name: inp_p90_ms
metrics.description: The 90th percentile Interaction to Next Paint time, in milliseconds. This shows the response time that 90% of measured page loads met or beat. Use `inp_p90_ms` to watch slower interaction experiences.

metrics.name: inp_p99_ms
metrics.description: The 99th percentile Interaction to Next Paint time, in milliseconds. This shows the response time that nearly all measured page loads met or beat. Use `inp_p99_ms` to investigate the slowest interaction experiences.

metrics.name: inp_poor_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a poor Interaction to Next Paint score. Poor INP means the page responded after more than 500 milliseconds. Use `inp_poor_view_count` to spot pages where interactions may feel slow.

metrics.name: lcp_distribution
metrics.description: A breakdown of page loads by Largest Contentful Paint, which measures how quickly the largest visible content appears. The values show measured loads, then good (2.5 seconds or faster), needs improvement (above 2.5 through 4 seconds), and poor (slower than 4 seconds). Use `lcp_distribution` to see how main content loading speed is spread across visits.

metrics.name: lcp_good_view_count

metrics.name: lcp_okay_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a Largest Contentful Paint score that needs improvement. This covers the largest visible content appearing after 2.5 seconds through 4 seconds. Use `lcp_okay_view_count` to find pages where main content could load faster.

metrics.name: lcp_p50_ms
metrics.description: The median Largest Contentful Paint time, in milliseconds. Half of measured page loads had the largest visible content appear at or below this value. Use `lcp_p50_ms` to track typical main content loading speed.

metrics.name: lcp_p75_ms
metrics.description: The 75th percentile Largest Contentful Paint time, in milliseconds. Most measured page loads had the largest visible content appear at or below this value. Use `lcp_p75_ms` to monitor main content loading for a broad share of visitors.

metrics.name: lcp_p90_ms
metrics.description: The 90th percentile Largest Contentful Paint time, in milliseconds. This shows the main content loading time that 90% of measured page loads met or beat. Use `lcp_p90_ms` to watch slower loading experiences.

metrics.name: lcp_p99_ms
metrics.description: The 99th percentile Largest Contentful Paint time, in milliseconds. This shows the main content loading time that nearly all measured page loads met or beat. Use `lcp_p99_ms` to investigate the slowest loading experiences.

metrics.name: lcp_poor_view_count
metrics.description: The number of page load events with a poor Largest Contentful Paint score. Poor LCP means the largest visible content appeared after more than 4 seconds. Use `lcp_poor_view_count` to spot pages with slow main content loading.

metrics.name: p50_cls
metrics.description: The median Cumulative Layout Shift score, which measures unexpected movement while the page loads. Half of measured page loads had a CLS score at or below this value. Use `p50_cls` to track typical layout stability.

metrics.name: p75_cls
metrics.description: The 75th percentile Cumulative Layout Shift score, which measures unexpected movement while the page loads. Most measured page loads had a CLS score at or below this value. Use `p75_cls` to monitor layout stability for a broad share of visitors.

metrics.name: p90_cls
metrics.description: The 90th percentile Cumulative Layout Shift score, which measures unexpected movement while the page loads. This shows the CLS score that 90% of measured page loads met or beat. Use `p90_cls` to watch less stable page experiences.

metrics.name: p99_cls
metrics.description: The 99th percentile Cumulative Layout Shift score, which measures unexpected movement while the page loads. This shows the CLS score that nearly all measured page loads met or beat. Use `p99_cls` to investigate the least stable experiences.

visualizationTypes.name: horizontal_bar
visualizationTypes.description: Lays bars out horizontally, which keeps long category labels readable. Use it for rankings or for categories with descriptive names, such as product or city titles.

visualizationTypes.name: horizontal_grouped_bar
visualizationTypes.description: Combines a horizontal layout with grouped series, so several metrics share each row. Use it when categories have long labels and need a side-by-side comparison.

visualizationTypes.name: single_stacked_bar
visualizationTypes.description: Shows one bar split into stacked segments, summarizing how a single total breaks down. Use it for a compact part-to-whole view, such as new and returning customers in a period.

visualizationTypes.name: stacked_bar
visualizationTypes.description: Stacks series on top of each other within each bar, showing both the category total and its composition. Use it to track how parts contribute to a whole across time or categories.

visualizationTypes.name: stacked_horizontal_bar
visualizationTypes.description: Stacks segments along horizontal bars, pairing part-to-whole composition with readable long labels. Use it when stacked categories have descriptive names.

visualizationTypes.name: rfm_grid
visualizationTypes.description: Arranges customer segments by recency, frequency, and monetary value. Use it to size and compare segments before targeting them.

visualizationTypes.name: bubble_chart
visualizationTypes.description: Positions points by two metrics and sizes each one by a third, packing three measures into a single view. Use it to compare entities across several dimensions at once.

visualizationTypes.name: histogram
visualizationTypes.description: Buckets values into ranges and shows how many records fall in each, revealing the shape of a distribution. Use it to understand frequency and spread, such as delivery times.

visualizationTypes.name: scatter_plot
visualizationTypes.description: Plots one metric against another as points, exposing correlation, clusters, and outliers. Use it to explore the relationship between two measures.

visualizationTypes.name: funnel
visualizationTypes.description: Shows how a count narrows across sequential stages, making the drop-off between steps obvious. Use it for conversion paths, such as sessions through to completed checkouts.

visualizationTypes.name: waterfall
visualizationTypes.description: Breaks a total into sequential positive and negative contributions, showing how you get from the starting value to the ending one. Use it to explain what drove a net change.

visualizationTypes.name: calendar_heatmap
visualizationTypes.description: Shades calendar days by intensity. Use it to find recurring weekly or seasonal hotspots.

visualizationTypes.name: heatmap
visualizationTypes.description: Shades a grid of two dimensions by value. Use it for patterns such as day of week against hour of day.

visualizationTypes.name: line
visualizationTypes.description: Connects values over time, making trends, peaks, and dips easy to follow. This is the default choice for time-series metrics.

visualizationTypes.name: stacked_area
visualizationTypes.description: Stacks filled series over time, showing both the running total and how each series contributes. Use it to track evolving composition across a period.

visualizationTypes.name: donut
visualizationTypes.description: Splits a total into proportional arcs around a ring, leaving the center open for a label or total. Use it for a quick part-to-whole read across a few categories.

visualizationTypes.name: sunburst
visualizationTypes.description: Renders a hierarchy as concentric rings radiating from a center, where each ring is one level deeper. Use it to explore nested categories and their contribution to the whole.

visualizationTypes.name: treemap
visualizationTypes.description: Tiles a rectangle into nested, area-sized boxes, packing many categories into a compact part-to-whole view. Use it to compare contribution across a large set of items.

visualizationTypes.name: radar
visualizationTypes.description: Plots several metrics on axes radiating from a center and connects them into a shape. Use it to contrast entities across multiple measures.

visualizationTypes.name: single_metric
visualizationTypes.description: Displays one headline number, optionally with a comparison to a prior period, instead of a chart. Use it to spotlight a single KPI.

visualizationTypes.name: list
visualizationTypes.description: Presents results as a simple ranked list of values, focused on the metric rather than on chart shape. Use it for compact rankings or feeds.

visualizationTypes.name: list_with_dimension_values
visualizationTypes.description: Lists results alongside their dimension values, keeping the breakdown labels next to each metric. Use it when those labels matter as much as the numbers.

visualizationTypes.name: table
visualizationTypes.description: Lays results out as rows and columns of exact values, supporting multiple metrics and dimensions. Use it when precise numbers matter more than visual shape.
